questions.q: Which part of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Rights?
questions.e: Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III (Articles 12–35).
questions.src: Constitution of India, Part III — Legislative Department, Government of India

questions.q: The idea of the Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.e: The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution of 1937.
questions.src: NCERT, Indian Constitution at Work; Constitution of India, Part IV

questions.q: Which Article guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws?
questions.e: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within India.

questions.q: Who described the Right to Constitutional Remedies as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar used this description for Article 32 in the Constituent Assembly.
questions.src: Constituent Assembly Debates; Constitution of India, Article 32

questions.q: Fundamental Duties are listed in which part of the Constitution?
questions.e: Part IVA contains Article 51A, which lists Fundamental Duties. They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
questions.src: Constitution of India, Part IVA; 42nd Amendment Act, 1976

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.e: The INC was founded in December 1885. Its first session was held in Bombay under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.
questions.src: NCERT, Themes in Indian History; Indian National Congress historical records

questions.q: Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.e: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session in 1885.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal announced in 1905 was carried out during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.e: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal in 1905; it was annulled in 1911.

questions.q: The Dandi March (Salt March) began in which year?
questions.e: Gandhi began the Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930, reaching Dandi in April.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in which year?
questions.e: The Quit India resolution was adopted at Bombay on 8 August 1942; the mass movement began the next day.

questions.q: Which blood cells are primarily responsible for transporting oxygen?
questions.e: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports oxygen.

questions.q: Which vitamin is essential for normal blood clotting?
questions.e: Vitamin K is required for the synthesis of several proteins involved in blood coagulation.

questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: Each kidney contains nephrons that filter blood and help form urine.

questions.q: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.e: Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.e: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, which can involve bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

questions.q: Which institution is India's central bank?
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India is the country's central bank and performs monetary and regulatory functions.

questions.q: GDP at market prices measures the value of:
o: Final goods and services produced within domestic territory
questions.e: GDP measures the value of final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory during a period.

questions.q: Which tax is generally classified as an indirect tax in India?
questions.e: GST is an indirect, destination-based tax levied on the supply of goods and services.

questions.q: The annual Union Budget is constitutionally referred to as the:
questions.e: Article 112 refers to the annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India.

questions.q: Repo rate is the rate at which:
o: RBI lends short-term funds to banks against eligible securities
Banks lend to one another without collateral
questions.e: The repo rate is the policy rate at which the RBI provides liquidity to banks against eligible collateral under the repo framework.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India began operations on:
questions.e: RBI commenced operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. It was nationalised in 1949.

questions.q: Which body regulates the securities market in India?
questions.e: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates the securities market and protects investors.

questions.q: NEFT stands for:
questions.e: NEFT is a nationwide centralised payment system operated by the RBI for transferring funds electronically.

questions.q: Which institution is primarily associated with agricultural and rural development finance?
questions.e: NABARD is the apex development financial institution for agriculture and rural development.

questions.q: DICGC deposit insurance currently covers eligible deposits up to what amount per depositor per bank, including principal and interest?
questions.e: DICGC insurance cover is up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, including principal and interest, subject to the applicable rules.
questions.src: DICGC — A Guide to Deposit Insurance

questions.q: Which memory is volatile?
questions.e: RAM is volatile memory: its contents are lost when power is switched off.

questions.q: What does URL stand for?
questions.e: URL means Uniform Resource Locator, the address used to locate a resource on the web.
questions.src: MDN Web Docs — What is a URL?

questions.q: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.e: Linux is an operating system kernel and forms the basis of many Linux distributions.

questions.q: In a spreadsheet, a formula generally begins with which symbol?
questions.e: In common spreadsheet applications such as LibreOffice Calc and Excel, formulas begin with an equals sign.

questions.q: Phishing is best described as:
o: A fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information by impersonation
questions.e: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to trick people into revealing credentials or other sensitive information.
